D: A Scottish commoner leads a rebellion against the English king.
P: Serve the mains when the Scots line up at Stirling.
S: Highland haggis bon bons, mustard cream
Spiced lamb and oat balls crumbed and fried crunchy, mustard cream dip, Stephen wants seconds.

Spiced lamb and oat haggis rolled into balls, crumbed and fried crunchy, with a wholegrain mustard and cream dipping sauce. Fry 400g lamb mince with a diced onion, then add 80g toasted oats, 1 tsp pepper, half a tsp nutmeg and 150ml beef stock and cook until thick. Cool and roll into 20 balls. Roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 175°C for 3 minutes until crisp. Simmer 150ml cream with 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard for 3 minutes for the dip.
Crisp Scottish oatcakes with sharp cheddar, sturdy enough for stone throwing.
Oatcakes of oats, butter, salt and hot water rolled thin, baked at 180C for 20 minutes, with sharp Scottish cheddar and apple chutney.
Smoked salmon squares, with Murron's thistle kept close.
Scottish smoked salmon on brown bread with lemon butter, dill and capers, cut into neat squares.
M: Lamb neck simmered with barley, split peas, leeks, carrots and turnip.
Lamb neck simmered 2 hours with pearl barley, split peas, leek, carrot and turnip, the meat pulled back in, parsley on top. Crusty bread.
Stirling venison with barley and kale
Backstrap seared rare and sliced over buttered barley and kale, with a peppery cream sauce.

Venison backstrap seared rare and sliced over buttered pearl barley and kale, with a peppery cream sauce. Simmer 250g pearl barley in salted water for 35 minutes until tender, then drain. Wilt 1 bunch shredded kale in 40g butter and stir through the barley. Season 800g venison backstrap with cracked pepper and sear in a hot pan 3 minutes a side for rare, then rest 8 minutes. Add 150ml cream and 1 tsp cracked pepper to the pan and simmer 2 minutes. Slice and spoon over.
W: Soft crowdie cheese whipped with heather honey, brambles and toasted oats.

Toast 60g rolled oats in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden, then cool. Beat 300g crowdie or ricotta with 3 tbsp heather honey until smooth. Layer into 4 glasses with 250g blackberries and the oats, finishing with a few berries and a drizzle of honey.
K: Honey mead warmed with clove and lemon peel, poured hot into cups.

Warm 750ml mead in a pan with 4 cloves and 2 strips of lemon peel until steaming, without boiling. Stir in 1 tbsp heather honey and pour into 4 heatproof cups. Leave out the mead and use cloudy apple juice for a hot spiced apple and honey.
